DESIGN_SYSTEM.LEAD: The shared design token foundation of the ng-hub-ui family: the CSS variables --hub-ref-* (primitives) and --hub-sys-* (semantic), with light/dark and 8 themes. Import it once and the whole family reads the same palette.

WHAT.TITLE: What it is and what it is for
WHAT.BODY: Its job is to unify and wire up the style variables across every library in the family. Each library is themed with --hub-* variables but does not define them: it consumes them. This package is the single source of truth that connects them, so that:
WHAT.LIST_1: One palette feeds panels, forms, calendar, board… at the same time.
WHAT.LIST_2: You re-theme once (one token) and the change reaches the whole family.
WHAT.LIST_3: Dark mode and 8 themes are ready, switchable with one attribute.
WHAT.LIST_4: You use it in your own CSS too, so your UI matches the components.
WHAT.NOTE: The wiring is rolling out library by library: further down, under the family, is the integration status of each one. Looking for the full token catalogue? It is in the token reference.

START.BODY: The whole route: what to install, what to import and where, and which mechanism to use for each kind of change. ds has no dependencies (plain CSS/SCSS) and emits nothing unless you import it.
START.STEP1_NOTE: ds is the base; add the family libraries you use. None of them defines the palette — they all consume the ds tokens.

START.STEP4_TITLE: 4 · And the rest of the libraries
START.STEP4_BODY: With the tokens loaded there is nothing else to configure: every ng-hub-ui-* reads --hub-sys-* and re-themes itself with your overrides. Each component also exposes --hub-<component>-* hooks for fine tuning, and some libraries ship sheets of their own, imported once next to the tokens — the exact path is documented by each README (the shared forms chrome, say, or the utils tooltip/overlay, as in the step 2 block). The integration status of every library is under the family.

ARCH.TITLE: Architecture: the two layers
ARCH.REF: Raw values with no context: colour ramps, spacing, radii, typography.
ARCH.SYS: Meaningful assignments, the ones components consume.
ARCH.RULE: Golden rule: components reference sys tokens only; sys points at ref. Changing a sys re-themes; changing a ref adjusts the base palette.

COLORS.TITLE: Semantic colours · live themes
COLORS.BODY: The set is open: 9 variants by default (5 chromatic + 4 neutral) plus the ones you add. Every accent exposes a uniform family of roles — subtle, border-subtle, emphasis and the contrast pair on. Switch the theme and watch the whole palette recolour.

BUILDER.TITLE: Build your theme · change the base colours only
BUILDER.BODY: Define only the base colour of each semantic family. The rest (subtle, border-subtle, emphasis, on) is derived automatically with color-mix / relative color — and the components below re-theme live, which is the shared wiring in action.

FAMILY.TITLE: The family · integration status
FAMILY.BODY: The whole family reads these tokens. The badge says whether a library is already wired to --hub-sys-* (it re-themes with the design system) or is still pending (we get to it later). Click any of them to see its examples.

MODIFY.ACCENT_TITLE: 2. Add an accent of your own
MODIFY.ACCENT_BODY: Define a --hub-sys-color-<name> family and the components that accept a semantic variant pick it up unchanged. Try it live here:
MODIFY.ACCENT_SAMPLE: brand alert — background, text and border derived from the accent with color-mix.
MODIFY.ACCENT_NOTE: --hub-sys-color-brand on its own already works (the components derive the rest with color-mix). Define the full family when you want exact tints.
MODIFY.OPEN_MAP_TITLE: … or predefine it in the open map (Sass)
MODIFY.OPEN_MAP_BODY: If you use Sass, extend the open accent map before including the package, with $hub-accents-extra. Only ds is recompiled — never the libraries — and every new variant gets its full family (subtle · border-subtle · emphasis · on):
MODIFY.THEME_TITLE: 3. Create a theme of your own
MODIFY.THEME_MIXIN_TITLE: 4. …or all of it at once with hub.theme() (Sass)
MODIFY.THEME_MIXIN_BODY: A single partial theming mixin: hand it only the changes as maps and it emits the variables under their canonical names. Everything hanging off each token — sys aliases, role families, utilities, components — re-derives on its own along the var() chain:

FUNCTIONS.TITLE: SCSS functions: how it is generated inside
FUNCTIONS.BODY: The semantic colour families are not written by hand: the accent set is an open map with !default and the family is derived with an @each over map.keys($hub-accents). That is why adding one colour (or nine) is uniform and free of boilerplate: every key in the map gets its family automatically.
FUNCTIONS.NOTE: For most cases you do not need to touch the SCSS: overriding CSS variables covers re-theming and adding accents. The map plus mixin is the internal machinery, useful if you contribute to the package.

STRUCTURE.TITLE: Structural layer · live tokens
STRUCTURE.BODY: Beyond colour, ds defines a canonical structural layer: the spacing scale (--hub-ref-space-*), sizing and fractions (--hub-sys-size-*), grid (--hub-sys-grid-columns, gutters) and a semantic gap scale (--hub-sys-gap-*). Everything below is painted by consuming those variables.

MIXINS.TITLE: Mixins and styles
MIXINS.BODY: The ds Sass API: helpers that consume the canonical tokens — with no spacing or colour baked in. They are imported namespaced, with @use 'ng-hub-ui-ds' as hub. The utility sheets are built from these same mixins, so changing or extending a behaviour means minting your own class with the mixin. Every demo below is built from the real mixin; the full catalogue is at the end.
MIXINS.NOTE: Every mixin has an equivalent utility; the demos below consume the real ds class (.cluster, .stack…) — this page re-applies no mixin.

UTILITIES.TITLE: Utilities
UTILITIES.BODY: Opt-in classes wrapping the same layer, under names exactly matching Bootstrap's — a drop-in replacement, but do not load these sheets AND Bootstrap globally in the same document. Three sheets: layout (display/flex, grid, spacing, sizing, position, helpers — these sections), text (the “Text” section) and surfaces (the “Surfaces” section). The demo uses the real classes:

FLEX.BODY: A complete set of display and flexbox utilities, under Bootstrap's exact naming. The demos use the real ds classes.
FLEX.RESPONSIVE_NOTE: The whole flex family has per-breakpoint variants. A column on mobile, a centred row from md up — resize the window:

TEXT.TITLE: Text
TEXT.BODY: Typography and text utilities under Bootstrap's exact naming, built on the typography mixins (hub.font-size(), hub.font-weight(), hub.text-color()…): every value resolves to tokens, so overriding the token re-themes the utilities — and with the mixins you can mint variants of your own.
TEXT.SIZE_NOTE: .fs-* changes the size only; .h1…6 applies a heading's full typography (size + bold + tight leading + margin) without the semantics — a <div class="h5"> reads like an <h5>:
TEXT.WEIGHT_SAMPLE: The weight comes from the token — {{weight}}
TEXT.TABULAR_BODY: Proportional figures give every digit its own width, so a 1 is narrower than a 0 and the units of two amounts land in different places. A column of money is read by comparing downwards: look at where the decimal separator falls on each side.
TEXT.TRUNCATE_SAMPLE: A text long enough not to fit into sixteen rem and to be truncated with an ellipsis.
TEXT.LH_SAMPLE: Two lines of text, enough to judge the leading each step of the scale applies.

SURFACES.TITLE: Surfaces
SURFACES.BODY: Backgrounds, borders, radii, shadows and opacity under Bootstrap's exact naming, built on the surface mixins (hub.bg(), hub.text-bg(), hub.radius(), hub.shadow()…) and the --hub-sys-color-* / --hub-sys-radius-* / --hub-sys-shadow-* tokens.

HELPERS.TITLE: Position and helpers
HELPERS.BODY: Position/inset, overflow, order, float, visibility, z-index, object-fit and interactions — plus the behavioural helpers (.visually-hidden, .stretched-link, .ratio-*, .clearfix). All under Bootstrap's exact naming.
HELPERS.OVERFLOW_SAMPLE: A block holding more content than fits: overflow-auto adds an inner scrollbar instead of spilling over the page layout.
HELPERS.FOCUS_NOTE: A focus ring driven by the --hub-sys-focus-ring-* tokens — click it or press Tab:
HELPERS.A11Y_NOTE: This paragraph holds a text hidden visually but announced by screen readers: for assistive technology only (inspect the DOM to see it).

BRIDGES.TITLE: Bridges to other systems
BRIDGES.BODY: Opt-in mixins that connect hub with whichever framework is present. Zero cost if you never call them. Two directions through $mode: adopt (hub takes the host's theme) and project (hub projects its theme onto the host).

CATALOG.THEME: Partial theming in one call: hand it only the changes as maps and it emits the canonical variables; whatever derives from them re-derives itself.
CATALOG.MEDIA_UP: Mobile-first media query from the breakpoint up (sm 576 · md 768 · lg 992 · xl 1200 · xxl 1400).
CATALOG.STACK: Flex column with a token gap.
CATALOG.GRID: Auto-fit grid with a minimum width per cell.
CATALOG.COL: Cell spanning $span tracks of a row().
CATALOG.OFFSET: Starts a col() on track $n + 1 (Bootstrap's offset); 0 resets it.
CATALOG.CENTER: Wrapper centred to a container max-width.
CATALOG.FONT_SIZE: 1–6 (heading scale) or xs | sm | base | lg.
CATALOG.TEXT_COLOR: An accent from the open map, body or muted; dimmed with --hub-text-opacity.
CATALOG.LINK_COLOR: Accent link with an -emphasis hover and an underline with opacity (--hub-link-underline-opacity).
CATALOG.TEXT_BREAK: Breaks long words and URLs instead of overflowing.
CATALOG.BG: Accent background (or its subtle tint), body or transparent; dimmed with --hub-bg-opacity.
CATALOG.TEXT_BG: Accent background + the -on colour with guaranteed contrast.
CATALOG.BORDER: Solid border with the default border token.
CATALOG.BORDER_COLOR: Border colour from an accent of the open map.
CATALOG.RADIUS: none | sm | md | lg | xl | xxl | pill | circle.
CATALOG.VISUALLY_HIDDEN: Hides it visually while keeping it available to screen readers.
CATALOG.STRETCHED_LINK: Extends the link's clickable area to its positioned ancestor.
CATALOG.BRIDGE_BOOTSTRAP: Adopts the --bs-* theme or projects onto it.
CATALOG.BRIDGE_OPEN_PROPS: Aliases of the Open Props ramps.

TEXT_FIELDS.TITLE: Text fields
TEXT_FIELDS.DESCRIPTION: The `hub-input` field with reactive-forms binding and automatic, zero-wiring error display. Text, email, password, number and counter, plus floating labels and input-group addons.

MULTILINE_RANGE.TITLE: Multiline & range
MULTILINE_RANGE.DESCRIPTION: Auto-growing textareas with character counters, and single / dual-thumb range sliders.

SELECTION.TITLE: Selection
SELECTION.DESCRIPTION: The forked ng-select engine themed with hub tokens, plus the button, radio and checkbox formats that render their own UI for the same value.

DATE_PICKING.TITLE: Date picking
DATE_PICKING.DESCRIPTION: A from-scratch date / range picker on native Date + CDK Overlay, with bounds, keyboard navigation and full i18n.

CONTAINERS_VALIDATION.TITLE: Containers & validation
CONTAINERS_VALIDATION.DESCRIPTION: `form[hubForm]`, `fieldset[hubFieldset]` / `hub-fieldset` and `hub-legend` surface group-level and form-level (cross-field) errors automatically — the same way fields surface control errors.

FILE_UPLOAD.TITLE: File upload
FILE_UPLOAD.DESCRIPTION: A file field with drag & drop, clipboard paste, type and size constraints, previews, and optional per-file upload progress.

RTL.TITLE: Right-to-left
RTL.DESCRIPTION: Every field mirrors under `dir="rtl"`. Most of that costs nothing — the primitives are written in logical CSS properties — but the slider, the switch and the segmented control needed explicit handling, because their geometry is only half CSS.

FORM_CONTROL_NAME.DESCRIPTION: Binds any field to a reactive control. Errors display automatically when the control is touched and invalid.

LABEL_TYPE.DESCRIPTION: Label placement. `floating` lays the label inside the control, where it stands in for the placeholder until the field is focused or holds a value.

FORM_TEXT.DESCRIPTION: Helper text shown below the control.

PASSWORD_REVEALED.DESCRIPTION: Two-way reveal state of a password field. Toggling the eye button updates it; setting it reveals or masks the value.

PASSWORD_TOGGLE.DESCRIPTION: Whether the integrated reveal toggle is rendered on password fields.

HIDE_ON_BLUR.DESCRIPTION: Whether a revealed password re-masks automatically when focus leaves the field.

CAPS_LOCK_WARNING.DESCRIPTION: Whether a hint is shown under the field while Caps Lock is active.

PASSWORD_STRENGTH.DESCRIPTION: Renders an opt-in 4-segment strength meter under the field. Scoring is overridable via provideHubForms.

AUTOCOMPLETE.DESCRIPTION: Native autocomplete attribute, e.g. current-password or new-password for password managers.

PREPEND_APPEND.DESCRIPTION: Static group addons on any field that renders as a box: a string is one addon, an array is a run of them, and empty entries are dropped rather than drawn as an empty box. The addon shares the field's border and is not focusable — for an interactive control attached to the edge, use the [hubPrepend] / [hubAppend] templates instead. Both can be present, and the projected content is always the outermost element on its side.

MASK.DESCRIPTION: Pattern mask for text formats. Tokens: 0 = digit, A = letter, * = alphanumeric; other chars are literal separators. E.g. "0000 0000 0000 0000".

UNMASK_VALUE.DESCRIPTION: With a mask set, store the raw typed characters (no separators) in the form instead of the formatted text.

RANGE.DESCRIPTION: Dual-thumb range slider; value becomes a [lower, upper] tuple.

FORMAT.DESCRIPTION: How the select renders the same value.

ITEMS.DESCRIPTION: Options, the label/value property names for object items, and multi-select.

ADD_TAG.DESCRIPTION: Create items from the search term (dropdown format): true adds the term as-is; a function maps the term to a new item, sync or Promise.

ADD_TAG_TEXT.DESCRIPTION: Label of the "add item" row shown while typing when addTag is enabled.

MIN_TERM_LENGTH.DESCRIPTION: Minimum search-term length before filtering (or the typeahead Subject) kicks in.

TYPEAHEAD.DESCRIPTION: Subject that receives search-term changes for async/server-side loading; when provided, client-side filtering switches off — feed the results back through items.

COMPARE_WITH.DESCRIPTION: Custom equality between an item and the bound value (e.g. objects compared by id); when omitted, the vendor's built-in comparison applies.

MODE.DESCRIPTION: Single date, a free date range, or one day with a start and end time within it.

MIN_MAX.DESCRIPTION: Selectable bounds and a per-date disabled predicate. The bounds honour the time, not just the day: a day is only disabled when no instant of it is allowed, so min = 2026-09-01T14:00 leaves 1 September clickable and the time controls refuse the earlier hours. Accepts an ISO string, a Date or epoch milliseconds.

CLEARABLE.DESCRIPTION: When true, shows an internal ✕ button once the field has a value; it resets the control and emits an empty search term.

INDETERMINATE.DESCRIPTION: When true, a checkbox shows the mixed state — the honest answer for a "select all" over a partially selected list. Two-way: the reader resolves it by clicking. Ignored by the switch format.

DEBOUNCE_TIME.DESCRIPTION: Debounce in milliseconds before the search event fires (0 = every keystroke).

OPTIONS.DESCRIPTION: The selectable options for hub-segmented, in render order — each { value, label, disabled? }.

SIZE.DESCRIPTION: Visual density of the segmented control: 'sm', 'md' (default) or 'lg'.

DISABLED.DESCRIPTION: Disables the field. Inherited by every field from the shared base, and two-way — a field disabled through its reactive control reports the change back. On `hub-segmented`, individual options can also opt out via `option.disabled`.

SEGMENTED_MULTIPLE.DESCRIPTION: Allow selecting more than one option; the value becomes an array and options toggle (aria-pressed).

SEGMENTED_VERTICAL.DESCRIPTION: Stack the segments vertically instead of in a horizontal row.

SEGMENTED_COLOR.DESCRIPTION: Semantic accent for the selected segment (primary, success, …) or any custom colour; slides in single mode.

FILE_MULTIPLE.DESCRIPTION: Whether more than one file can be held. Switches the control value from File to File[].

FILE_ACCEPT.DESCRIPTION: Accepted file types, e.g. image/*,.pdf. Enforced on drops and pastes, not just in the OS dialog.

FILE_SIZES.DESCRIPTION: Per-file maximum and minimum size, and the maximum combined size, in bytes.

FILE_MAX_FILES.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of files. Only meaningful together with multiple.

FILE_DRAG_DROP.DESCRIPTION: Whether files can be dropped onto the field, and whether they can be pasted into it.

FILE_PREVIEW.DESCRIPTION: How the held files are rendered: not at all, as a list, as tiles under the dropzone (grid), or as tiles inside the field (inline). An inline tile alone fills the field; with multiple, the tiles form a grid ending in an add tile.

FILE_ALLOW_DUPLICATES.DESCRIPTION: Whether the same file can be selected twice (keyed on name, size and last-modified date).

FILE_CAPTURE.DESCRIPTION: Opens the device camera instead of the file browser, on the platforms that support it.

FILE_AUTO_UPLOAD.DESCRIPTION: Whether a newly accepted file starts uploading immediately. Ignored when no uploader is registered.

FILE_BUTTON_LABEL.DESCRIPTION: Overrides the browse-button text and the auto-generated constraints hint.

FILE_DROP_TEXT.DESCRIPTION: Per-instance overrides for the two invitation lines of the dropzone. Both fall back to the global labels.

GROUP_BY.DESCRIPTION: Property name (dot path) used to group the dropdown items under option-group headers.

SEARCHABLE_CLEARABLE.DESCRIPTION: Whether the options can be filtered by typing (searchable) and whether the selection can be cleared with the built-in clear button (clearable). Both default to true.

CLOSE_ON_SELECT.DESCRIPTION: Whether the dropdown closes after selecting an item. Set to false to keep it open while picking several values in multiple mode.

FIXED_PLACEHOLDER.DESCRIPTION: Keep the placeholder visible even when a value is selected. Defaults to false (the placeholder hides on selection), inverting ng-select v23's unconventional default.

LOADING_NOT_FOUND.DESCRIPTION: loading renders the dropdown's loading state while async items are being fetched; notFoundText is the message shown when no items match the search term.

SELECT_READONLY.DESCRIPTION: When true, the field displays its value but rejects any interaction, without the disabled styling or form-state change.

APPEND_TO.DESCRIPTION: CSS selector of the element the dropdown panel is appended to. Defaults to 'body' so the panel escapes overflow/transform ancestors (cards, scroll containers, modals); pass undefined to render it inline.

SEGMENTED_VALUE.DESCRIPTION: Two-way bindable selected value (model()): the chosen option's value in single mode, an array of selected values in multiple mode. Emits valueChange; normally driven through formControlName instead.

DATEPICKER_LOCALE.DESCRIPTION: Calendar i18n: locale is the BCP-47 tag for the display value and month/weekday names (defaults to the app's LOCALE_ID, falling back to en-US); firstDayOfWeek sets the first weekday (0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday…); weekdayFormat picks the weekday header width. The last two fall back to the global provideHubForms config.

DATEPICKER_FORMAT.DESCRIPTION: Display formatting: displayFormat renders the selected value and accepts Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions, an Angular date pattern such as 'dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm', or a function; timeDisplayFormat is composed over it once the granularity carries a time, so the date part keeps whatever displayFormat said; rangeSeparator is the text between the two dates of a range; and labels overrides the picker's UI labels per instance (merged over the global config).

DATEPICKER_BEHAVIOR.DESCRIPTION: Behavior flags: clearable shows the clear shortcut, showToday shows the "today" shortcut, and closeOnSelect closes the calendar after picking a date (single mode only). Defaults: true / true / true.

DATEPICKER_GRANULARITY.DESCRIPTION: Precision each picked point carries, and the panel that picks it: year and month render a 12-cell period grid, day the calendar, and hour, minute and second add a time strip to it. Orthogonal to mode — mode says how many points are picked, granularity how precise each one is. Defaults to day, which emits the same YYYY-MM-DD string as before; from hour onwards the value is a full ISO 8601 timestamp carrying the reader's local wall clock and the offset of that date.

DATEPICKER_VALUE_FORMAT.DESCRIPTION: The value axes. valueFormat sets what the bound control holds: 'iso' (the default), 'date' for a native Date, 'timestamp' for epoch milliseconds, or a function for anything else. parse sets how an incoming value is read, overriding the built-in detection of ISO strings of any width, Date instances and epoch milliseconds — and it applies to min and max too.

DATEPICKER_TIME.DESCRIPTION: Time controls: minuteStep and secondStep are the spinbutton increments, and hourFormat forces a 12- or 24-hour clock — derived from the locale when unset, and applied to the input display as well as to the panel, so the two can never disagree. All three fall back to the global provideHubForms config.

CLASSLIST.DESCRIPTION: Extra CSS classes applied to the host element.

FORM_TEXT_TYPE.DESCRIPTION: Where the helper text is shown: `bottom` (the default) draws it under the control, `tooltip` puts it behind a question mark at the end of the label row. The rule this settles is one sentence below, more than one in the tooltip — a paragraph under every field turns a form into a document. The trigger is a button beside the label, never inside it, so opening it does not also focus the control, and its accessible name is the helper text itself.

COLS.DESCRIPTION: Number of visible columns. When set, the textarea stops stretching to full width.

MAXLENGTH.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of characters. Drives both the native limit and the counter.

COUNTER.DESCRIPTION: Whether to show a character counter below the control.

AUTORESIZE.DESCRIPTION: Whether the textarea grows to fit its content.

LENGTH.DESCRIPTION: Number of cells / characters in the code.

SECRET.DESCRIPTION: Masks the characters like a password.

SEPARATOR.DESCRIPTION: The separator character shown between groups.

SEPARATOR_EVERY.DESCRIPTION: Inserts a visual separator every N cells (0 = none).

SHOW_VALUE.DESCRIPTION: Whether to show the value bubble(s) above the thumb(s).

LEGEND.DESCRIPTION: Legend text. Ignored when a `hubLegend` template is projected.

REQUIRED_LEGEND.DESCRIPTION: Whether to render the required indicator.

INVALID_LEGEND.DESCRIPTION: Whether to render the invalid state styling.

LABEL_TYPE_STACKED_ONLY.DESCRIPTION: Label placement. These fields have no floating variant: passed `floating`, they render a stacked label.

SELECT_VERTICAL.DESCRIPTION: Deprecated, and tied to the deprecated non-dropdown formats: lays the buttons/checkbox/radio options out vertically. Use `<hub-segmented [vertical]="true">`.

SEARCH_FN.DESCRIPTION: Replaces the built-in matching used by `searchable`. Receives the typed term and an item, and returns whether the item matches — so a search can look at fields the label does not show.

SHOW_VALID.DESCRIPTION: Whether a valid field shows its valid state. Off by default because a form that paints every untouched field green says nothing; the invalid state is always shown.

VALID_FEEDBACK.DESCRIPTION: Message rendered under the field once it is valid, when `showValid` is on.

INVALID_FEEDBACK_TEMPLATE_FN.DESCRIPTION: Overrides the message for a given error key on this field alone. Receives the error key and its value, and returns the text — the app-wide default lives in `provideHubForms`.

INPUT_MIN_MAX.DESCRIPTION: Numeric bounds for the number and counter formats. Two-way, so a counter that clamps its own value reports the bound back.

OTP_MODE.DESCRIPTION: Which characters a box accepts, and which keyboard a phone offers: digits only, or letters and digits.

TIMEPICKER_MIN_MAX.DESCRIPTION: Earliest and latest time the field accepts, as `HH:MM`. Empty means unbounded.

TIMEPICKER_STEP.DESCRIPTION: Granularity of the native stepper, in seconds. `0` leaves the browser default of one minute.

GROUP.DESCRIPTION: The group whose errors the container surfaces. Give `group` an `AbstractControl` directly, or `groupName` the name of a child of the surrounding form — neither is needed when the container already wraps the group it reports on.

ERROR_TRIGGER.DESCRIPTION: When group-level errors become visible: once the group has been touched, only after a submit attempt, or immediately.

REQUIRED_ALL.DESCRIPTION: Whether the field is required. With a reactive binding it is derived from the control’s own validators, so setting it inline is only honoured for template-driven fields; it drives the asterisk and the `required` attribute.

DATEPICKER_MONTH_FORMAT.DESCRIPTION: How the panel's header names the month. Abbreviated by default, because the panel is exactly as wide as the day grid and the header takes what the nav buttons leave — 102px, where a spelled-out «septiembre de 2026» needs 152 and would be cut off. Ask for `long` where you have widened the panel, through `--hub-daterangepicker-cell-size` or `--hub-datepicker-grid-gap`. Widening is global: the calendar renders in an overlay attached to `document.body`, so a custom property set on the field never reaches it — declare the tokens at `:root`.

PLAINTEXT.DESCRIPTION: The value with no field around it. `readonly` is a state of a field somebody is still filling in, and a theme gives it a box through `--hub-input-readonly-bg` / `-border-color`; `plaintext` is for a value merely being shown, and having no box is what it is rather than a colour it wears. At the shipped defaults `readonly` draws no box either, so untouched the two differ in horizontal padding, inline border width, cursor and affordances. Implies `readonly`, and the two presentations are exclusive. The control stays a real input, so the label still labels it and the text stays selectable.

SLIDER_MIN_MAX.DESCRIPTION: Bounds of the range the thumb travels. The increment is set by step; on a dual-thumb slider both thumbs share these bounds.

INPUT_FILE_DEPRECATED.DESCRIPTION: Left over from hub-input's deprecated file format. Still public and still honoured, but file picking lives in hub-file-input now, which enforces accept on drops and pastes and not only in the OS dialog. Removed in the next major.

HUB_AUTORESIZE.DESCRIPTION: Standalone directive for a plain textarea: it grows the element to fit its content. hub-textarea applies it itself through its own autoresize input; this is how to reach it on a textarea the library does not own.

FILE_CURRENT_FILE.DESCRIPTION: Files the record already has, shown by preview="inline": a URL, a HubCurrentFile { url, name?, type? }, or with multiple a list of either. Display only: they never enter the form value.

FILE_IMAGE_PREVIEW.DESCRIPTION: Whether images are shown as images. Off, every file is drawn as its family icon and no object URL is created for a thumbnail.

FILE_READONLY.DESCRIPTION: The files stay in view and can be opened, but none can be picked, dropped, pasted, replaced or removed. Unlike disabled, the field keeps its focus and is submitted.

FILE_CLEARABLE.DESCRIPTION: Whether the user may remove what the field holds, picked or stored. Also governs the remove buttons and Remove all of list and grid.

COLOR_SWATCHES.DESCRIPTION: Colours offered by type="color" as a grid of swatches: CSS colour strings or { value, label }. null takes the palette from provideHubForms({ color }), or the classic hex field when there is none; [] forces the classic field. HUB_COLOR_PALETTES has five ready-made lists.

COLOR_ALLOW_CUSTOM.DESCRIPTION: Whether the swatch grid ends with a cell that opens the native picker for a colour outside the list. Turn it off for a closed palette.

COLOR_CUSTOM_LABEL.DESCRIPTION: Accessible name of the custom-colour cell. Empty falls back to color.customColorLabel in the global config.

VALUE_CHANGE.DESCRIPTION: Emits whenever the field value changes.

SUBMIT.DESCRIPTION: Not a custom output: `hubForm` listens to the form’s own `submit` event, prevents the default navigation, marks the tree as touched and flips the submitted state. Bind `(submit)` on the form for your own handler.

SEARCH.DESCRIPTION: Debounced typeahead term emitted as the user types (text-like inputs).

REJECTED.DESCRIPTION: The files refused by the declared constraints, each with the reason for its rejection.

FILE_REMOVED.DESCRIPTION: A picked file that left the selection: removed, or replaced through its tile.

UPLOAD_STATE_CHANGE.DESCRIPTION: The full item list whenever an upload changes status or progress.

ON_FOCUS_BLUR.DESCRIPTION: Emit when the dropdown control gains or loses focus (dropdown format), relaying the vendor's focus/blur events.

SCROLL.DESCRIPTION: scroll emits the visible { start, end } window while the dropdown list scrolls; scrollToEnd emits when the list reaches its end — the hook for infinite/paged loading with typeahead.

ENTER.DESCRIPTION: Emits the current value when Enter is pressed.

COMPLETED.DESCRIPTION: Emits the full code once every cell is filled.

MODEL_CHANGE.DESCRIPTION: Every two-way `model()` input publishes a matching `Change` output, so `[(disabled)]` and friends work. They are listed here because the banana-in-a-box syntax hides them.

CURRENT_FILE_REMOVED.DESCRIPTION: A stored file (currentFile) that left the field: removed, or replaced by a picked file. The form value never held it, so this is the cue to delete it on the server.

1.NAME: hubValidationError
1.DESCRIPTION: Override the message for a given error key.

2.NAME: hub-legend
2.DESCRIPTION: The fieldset's legend, projected as an element — it carries the required marker and the invalid state.

3.NAME: hubSelectOption (hub-select)
3.DESCRIPTION: Custom dropdown option rendering. One of the hubSelect* slots — hubSelectLabel, hubSelectHeader, hubSelectFooter, hubSelectNotFound and the rest cover the other parts of the panel.

4.NAME: hubFileIcon (hub-file-input)
4.DESCRIPTION: Per-file glyph for files with no thumbnail; receives the item as implicit context.

5.NAME: hubFilePreview (hub-file-input)
5.DESCRIPTION: Replaces the whole rendering of a selected file, receiving the item plus the remove, retry and cancel actions.

6.NAME: hubFileDropzoneNotice (hub-file-input)
6.DESCRIPTION: Projects arbitrary markup at the top of the dropzone, above the glyph — for a notice the invitation and the constraints hint cannot express.

7.NAME: hubSegmentedOption (hub-segmented)
7.DESCRIPTION: Replaces each segment's content (icons, badges, rich markup) while the component keeps owning selection, keyboard navigation and ARIA. Context: the option (implicit), selected and index.

8.NAME: hubSelectSuffix (hub-select, deprecated)
8.DESCRIPTION: Deprecated since 22.16.0 — use [hubAppend], which does the same on every field. It keeps working; [hubAppend] wins if both are present. Attaches an interactive control to the select's inline-end edge — a button that acts on whatever is selected: configure it, look it up, create a new one. Declared as a template rather than projected content because the select's catch-all ng-content carries ng-option through to the engine and would swallow it; rendering from a template also keeps the action after the control in the DOM, so tabbing reaches the field before the button acting on it. The control and the action share one border and read as a single field.

9.NAME: hubPrepend / hubAppend (all box-shaped fields)
9.DESCRIPTION: Content attached to a field's edge, richer than the text a prepend / append string can carry: an icon, or a button that acts on the value. Available on every field that renders as a box with a value — hub-input, hub-select, hub-textarea and hub-datepicker. Composes with the string addons rather than replacing them: the strings render first, so projected content is always the outermost element on its side — a unit labels the field, the action sits beyond it. Whatever is projected wears the field's border, radius and height rather than its own, so a button does not draw a second, thicker seam beside the control. Declared as a template because a field's ng-content is already spoken for. A slot can also hand over another field — hub-input, hub-select, hub-textarea or hub-datepicker as a direct child — which closes flush against the host so that a price and the period it is a price of read as the one statement they are.

10.NAME: hubInputPrefix / hubInputSuffix (hub-input)
10.DESCRIPTION: Projects content into the field’s inline-start or inline-end affix area — a leading icon, a currency symbol, an inline SVG. Attribute directives rather than templates: put them on the projected element itself. The field reserves the inline padding, so its text never runs under the affix, and themes a projected hub-icon with its --hub-input-icon-* tokens. Both edges follow the writing direction, so they flip under dir="rtl". For a clear button, prefer the built-in clearable input.

SLIDER_TRACK_FILL_BG.DESCRIPTION: Filled portion of the slider track.

DATERANGEPICKER_PREVIEW_BG.DESCRIPTION: Background of the tentative range band, previewed while an end date is being chosen.

INPUT_ICON_COLOR.DESCRIPTION: Color of the in-field icon affix.

INPUT_ICON_SIZE.DESCRIPTION: Size of the in-field icon affix.

INPUT_CLEAR_ICON.DESCRIPTION: Clear (✕) button glyph, as a mask image — swap it to restyle the icon.

INPUT_CLEAR_HOVER_COLOR.DESCRIPTION: Clear button color on hover / focus.

INPUT_PASSWORD.TITLE: Password fields — toggle, strength meter & autocomplete

INPUT_COLOR_SWATCHES.TITLE: Color swatches — a palette the size of a field

FIELD_ATTACHED.TITLE: Icons, buttons and fields attached to a field

FILE_INPUT_INLINE.TITLE: Inline preview — the file inside the field

FORM_TEXT_TOOLTIP.TITLE: Helper text: below or behind a mark

LABEL_VISUALLY_HIDDEN.TITLE: Clipped labels: named without being drawn

MANUAL_COMMITS_AND_TIME_TRAVEL.TITLE: Manual Commits and Time Travel
MANUAL_COMMITS_AND_TIME_TRAVEL.DESCRIPTION: Track state changes and travel backwards/forwards through linear history.
MANUAL_COMMITS_AND_TIME_TRAVEL.HIGHLIGHT: Commit a snapshot when it matters and walk the linear timeline with undo() and redo().

NESTED_OBJECTS_AND_ARRAYS.TITLE: Nested Objects and Arrays
NESTED_OBJECTS_AND_ARRAYS.DESCRIPTION: Use patch-based tracking for deep object graphs and list mutations.
NESTED_OBJECTS_AND_ARRAYS.HIGHLIGHT: Entries keep forward and backward diff patches, so deep objects and list edits cost bytes rather than full copies.

AUTOMATIC_FORM_TRACKING.TITLE: Automatic Form Tracking
AUTOMATIC_FORM_TRACKING.DESCRIPTION: Auto-commit form value changes with built-in watch helpers.
AUTOMATIC_FORM_TRACKING.HIGHLIGHT: watchForm() commits every FormGroup value change and hands back the function that stops it.

TRANSACTIONS_AND_RETENTION.TITLE: Transactions and Retention
TRANSACTIONS_AND_RETENTION.DESCRIPTION: Group multiple operations into one entry and trim old entries by configured limits.
TRANSACTIONS_AND_RETENTION.HIGHLIGHT: Collapse a batch of commits into one entry and cap what is kept by entry count or approximate bytes.

CREATE_HISTORY_STORE.DESCRIPTION: Factory that creates a signal-based history store tracking multiple objects by id. Accepts optional retention limits (maxEntries, default 100; maxBytes, default 512000), a keySelector, and custom diff/patch strategies.

STATES.DESCRIPTION: Computed signal exposing a map of the current immutable state snapshots keyed by object id.

REGISTER_OBJECT.DESCRIPTION: Registers a tracked object with its initial state and starts a fresh, empty history timeline for that id.

REGISTER_FROM_OBJECT.DESCRIPTION: Registers a tracked object deriving its id from the configured keySelector and returns that id. Throws when no keySelector was configured.

COMMIT.DESCRIPTION: Commits a new state snapshot for a registered id, storing forward and backward patches and discarding any redo entries ahead of the pointer. Returns false when the new state produces no changes. Inside an open transaction it only updates the current state without creating an entry.

COMMIT_FROM_OBJECT.DESCRIPTION: Commits a new state deriving the id from the configured keySelector. Throws when no keySelector was configured.

UNDO.DESCRIPTION: Reverts one history step by applying the entry's backward patch. Returns false when there is nothing to undo.

REDO.DESCRIPTION: Re-applies one history step by applying the entry's forward patch. Returns false when there is nothing to redo.

CAN_UNDO.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether undo is currently possible for the given object id.

CAN_REDO.DESCRIPTION: Returns whether redo is currently possible for the given object id.

GET_STATE.DESCRIPTION: Returns a deep clone of the current state for the given id, or undefined when the id is not registered.

HISTORY.DESCRIPTION: Returns readonly metadata for the object's history: the pointer, entry count, approximate retained bytes, and per-entry label, timestamp, and bytes.

BEGIN_TRANSACTION.DESCRIPTION: Starts a transaction so subsequent commits are collapsed into a single consolidated history entry. Throws when a transaction is already open for the id.

END_TRANSACTION.DESCRIPTION: Ends the open transaction, committing one consolidated entry from the transaction start state to the current state. Returns false when no transaction was open or no changes were made.

WATCH_FORM.DESCRIPTION: Subscribes to a FormGroup's valueChanges and automatically commits each emission, optionally skipping the initial one. Returns an unsubscribe callback.

STATE_LABEL.DESCRIPTION: The word this node is announced with, clipped out of the page and read out with the step. Overrides the application-wide `stateLabels` from `provideHubMilestones`; `''` silences this node, and leaving it unset inherits the configured wording (English by default: Completed, Pending, Error, and nothing for active, which `aria-current="step"` already names).

ANIMATION.DESCRIPTION: If true, modal opening and closing will be animated. Default: true

BACKDROP.DESCRIPTION: If true, the backdrop element will be created. Alternatively, specify "static" for a backdrop which doesn't close the modal on click. Default: true

CENTERED.DESCRIPTION: If true, the modal will be centered vertically. Default: false

PLACEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Controls where the modal is placed within the viewport. Default: HubModalPlacement.Center

KEYBOARD.DESCRIPTION: If true, the modal will be closed when Escape key is pressed. Default: true

WINDOWCLASS.DESCRIPTION: A custom class to append to the modal window

BACKDROPCLASS.DESCRIPTION: A custom class to append to the modal backdrop

DISMISSSELECTOR.DESCRIPTION: Custom selector for elements that can trigger the dismissal of the modal window. Default: "[data-dismiss=\"modal\"]"

CLOSESELECTOR.DESCRIPTION: Custom selector for elements that can trigger the closing of the modal window. Default: "[data-close=\"modal\"]"

HEADERSELECTOR.DESCRIPTION: Custom selector for the header element of the modal window

FOOTERSELECTOR.DESCRIPTION: Custom selector for the footer element of the modal window

DATA.DESCRIPTION: Additional data that needs to be passed to the modal window when it is opened

OFFCANVAS.DESCRIPTION: Opens the dialog as a drawer: flush against the edge named by `placement`, square on that side, stretched to the full height (or width, from the top or bottom), and scrolling in the body so the header and footer stay put. Its width comes from `--hub-modal-offcanvas-width`, not from the size scale — `size: 'lg'` is 800px, which on a narrow window covers the document the drawer is meant to be read against. With no `placement` it opens from the end edge, so a drawer is one decision. Separate from `placement` on purpose: an edge placement alone still gives the floating dialog it always gave.

VARIANT.DESCRIPTION: Semantic accent of the dialog, for one that means something — a destructive confirmation, a success notice. It re-bases the single `--hub-modal-accent` slot, and the emphasis / subtle / on / border roles derive from it on the dialog itself, so one value recolours the tinted background, the outer edge with its header and footer rules, and the title. The stylesheet ships nine: `primary`, `secondary`, `success`, `danger`, `warning`, `info`, `neutral`, `light` and `dark`. Any other string is accepted as well and applies `hub-modal--<name>` to the window, so a custom accent costs one rule in a global stylesheet and no recompilation. A top accent bar belongs to the set too, but ships at zero width: set `--hub-modal-accent-bar-width` on the dialog to turn it on. Without a variant the dialog stays neutral.

ARIALABELLEDBY.DESCRIPTION: ID of the element that labels the dialog. Applied as `aria-labelledby` on the modal window.

ARIADESCRIBEDBY.DESCRIPTION: ID of the element that describes the dialog. Applied as `aria-describedby` on the modal window.

CLOSEARIALABEL.DESCRIPTION: Accessible name of the dismiss button the library draws in its own header. That button carries no text — its glyph is painted by CSS — so this string is the whole of what a screen reader announces: pass the translated string here, or set the default once on `HubModalConfig`. Default: "Close"

BEFOREDISMISS.DESCRIPTION: Guard called right before the modal is dismissed. Return `false`, a promise resolved with `false`, or a rejected promise, and the dialog stays open.

CONTAINER.DESCRIPTION: CSS selector or element the modal windows are appended to. Default: `body`

FULLSCREEN.DESCRIPTION: `true` keeps the dialog fullscreen at every width; a breakpoint name such as `"md"` only below that width. Any other string applies `modal-fullscreen-<value>-down`. Default: false

INJECTOR.DESCRIPTION: Injector used to resolve the dependencies of the content component.

SCROLLABLE.DESCRIPTION: Pins the dialog and scrolls its body, instead of letting the dialog grow past the viewport. Default: false

MODALDIALOGCLASS.DESCRIPTION: A custom class to append to the `hub-modal__dialog` element

BODYSELECTOR.DESCRIPTION: CSS selector for the block whose children become the body. Without it the body is whatever the header and the footer left behind, which depends on the order the content is written in; with it the body is placed deliberately, and anything no slot claimed still follows it.

0.NAME: Modal Template
0.DESCRIPTION: Template reference that can be passed to the modal service. The header, body and footer blocks become slots only when `headerSelector`, `bodySelector` and `footerSelector` are given on `open()`; without them the whole template lands in the body.

DISMISS.DESCRIPTION: Emitted by the modal window when the user dismisses the modal, e.g. by pressing Escape, clicking the backdrop, or activating the built-in close button. The payload is the dismiss reason (ModalDismissReasons.ESC, ModalDismissReasons.BACKDROP_CLICK, or a custom value).

OPEN.DESCRIPTION: Opens a new modal window with the given content (component type, TemplateRef, or string) and options, and returns a HubModalRef to control it. Content components can inject HubActiveModal and the HUB_MODAL_DATA token to interact with the modal and read the data payload.

DISMISS_ALL.DESCRIPTION: Dismisses all currently displayed modal windows with the supplied reason.

HAS_OPEN_MODALS.DESCRIPTION: Indicates if there are currently any open modal windows in the application.

ACTIVE_INSTANCES.DESCRIPTION: Event emitter that emits the list of currently open HubModalRef instances every time a modal is opened or removed.

REF_CLOSE.DESCRIPTION: Closes the modal with an optional result value. The HubModalRef.result promise is resolved with the provided value.

REF_DISMISS.DESCRIPTION: Dismisses the modal with an optional reason value. The HubModalRef.result promise is rejected with the provided value. Honours the beforeDismiss guard when one was configured.

REF_UPDATE.DESCRIPTION: Updates options of an opened modal (aria attributes, centered, placement, fullscreen, backdropClass, size, variant, windowClass, modalDialogClass).

REF_COMPONENT_INSTANCE.DESCRIPTION: The instance of the component used as modal content. Returns undefined when a TemplateRef was used as content or when the modal is closed.

REF_RESULT.DESCRIPTION: Promise resolved with the close result when the modal is closed and rejected with the dismiss reason when it is dismissed.

REF_CLOSED.DESCRIPTION: Observable that emits the result passed to close() when the modal is closed.

REF_DISMISSED.DESCRIPTION: Observable that emits the dismiss reason when the modal is dismissed — the value passed to dismiss(), or an internal reason such as backdrop click or Escape.

REF_SHOWN.DESCRIPTION: Observable that emits and completes once the modal is fully visible and its opening animation has finished.

REF_HIDDEN.DESCRIPTION: Observable that emits and completes once both the modal window and the backdrop are hidden, animations finished, and their elements removed from the DOM.

ACTIVE_CLOSE.DESCRIPTION: Closes the modal hosting the content component, resolving the HubModalRef.result promise with the optional result value.

ACTIVE_DISMISS.DESCRIPTION: Dismisses the modal hosting the content component, rejecting the HubModalRef.result promise with the optional reason value.

ACTIVE_UPDATE.DESCRIPTION: Updates options of the opened modal from inside the content component.

ACTIVE_DATA.DESCRIPTION: The typed payload passed through HubModalOptions.data. Equivalent to injecting the HUB_MODAL_DATA token; resolves to null when no data option was provided.

PANEL_DRILL_DOWN.DESCRIPTION: Stacked panel navigation where clicking a dropdown opens its children in a side panel. Supports configurable max panels, drill-down with back navigation, and left/right sidebar positioning.

ITEMS.DESCRIPTION: Array of navigation items to render. Each item defines its type (link, dropdown, header, separator, custom), label, route, icon, badge, children, and more.

CONFIG.DESCRIPTION: Partial configuration overrides merged with global defaults. Controls orientation, dropdown trigger, collapse mode, breakpoint, position, and more.

ITEM_TEMPLATE.DESCRIPTION: Optional custom template for rendering nav items via input binding. The hubNavItemTemplate directive takes priority over this input.

AUTO_OPEN_FROM_ROUTE.DESCRIPTION: When true, the nav automatically opens the dropdowns and drill-down panels matching the active router URL on initialization and after every navigation. Useful for sidebar navigations where the URL drives the open state. In a menu whose roots expand in different ways only one section stays open: arriving at an accordion root closes the panel of the panel root you left, and the other way round.

COLOR.DESCRIPTION: Semantic accent applied to hover/active affordances. Accepts a semantic name (primary, success, danger, warning, info), a registered accent name, a CSS named colour, or a literal #hex / rgb() / oklch() / var(). Barewords resolve to the --hub-sys-color-<name> token; defaults to primary when omitted.

RAIL.DESCRIPTION: Desktop-only icon rail. When true, a vertical nav renders at rail width showing icons only. Ignored below collapseBreakpoint, where the offcanvas behavior always wins. Two-way bindable via [(rail)].

CONFIG_ORIENTATION.DESCRIPTION: Orientation of the navigation: horizontal renders a top bar, vertical renders a sidebar.

CONFIG_VERTICAL_EXPAND_MODE.DESCRIPTION: How child items expand in vertical orientation: accordion expands inline, flyout opens a positioned side submenu, panel opens stacked drill-down panels.

CONFIG_DROPDOWN_TRIGGER.DESCRIPTION: Mechanism that opens dropdown menus: on hover, on click, or both.

CONFIG_DROPDOWN_RENDER_MODE.DESCRIPTION: Rendering strategy for dropdown and flyout menus: inline inside the nav DOM, or overlay in a body-level layer to avoid clipping. Panel drill-down mode is not affected.

CONFIG_POSITION.DESCRIPTION: CSS positioning strategy for the nav container. Sticky positioning is only activated for vertical navigation.

CONFIG_STICKY_TOP.DESCRIPTION: Top offset used when sticky positioning is enabled. Accepts any valid CSS length value.

CONFIG_COLLAPSE_MODE.DESCRIPTION: Display mode when the menu collapses on small viewports: offcanvas slide-in drawer, dropdown below the toggler, or fullscreen overlay.

CONFIG_COLLAPSE_BREAKPOINT.DESCRIPTION: Viewport width in pixels below which the menu collapses. Set to 0 to disable responsive collapsing.

CONFIG_OFFCANVAS_POSITION.DESCRIPTION: Side from which the offcanvas panel slides in. Only applies when collapseMode is offcanvas.

CONFIG_ARIA_LABEL.DESCRIPTION: Accessible label applied to the nav element.

CONFIG_PANEL_MAX_VISIBLE.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of simultaneously visible panels in panel expand mode. Beyond it, the last panel drills down in place with back navigation.

CONFIG_SIDEBAR_SIDE.DESCRIPTION: Physical side of the sidebar: left (panels extend to the right) or right (panels extend to the left).

CONFIG_PANEL_WIDTH.DESCRIPTION: Width of each drill-down panel. Accepts any valid CSS width value.

CONFIG_RAIL_TOGGLE.DESCRIPTION: Whether the built-in edge toggle renders on the primary column of a vertical desktop nav. Disable it when the app ships its own toggle. Fully themeable through the --hub-nav-rail-toggle-* tokens, including a replaceable SVG arrow.

CONFIG_LABELS.DESCRIPTION: Per-instance overrides for the built-in accessible labels. Omitted labels resolve from the shared HUBUI.NAV.* dictionary keys, then from the English defaults.

SCROLL_SPY_SECTION_SELECTOR.DESCRIPTION: CSS selector used to locate trackable section elements inside the host container.

SCROLL_SPY_SECTION_ID.DESCRIPTION: Optional section id for a tracked section. When omitted, the host element id attribute is used.

SUB_NAV_ITEM.DESCRIPTION: The navigation item rendered by the internal hub-nav-item child. Managed automatically by hub-nav; rarely bound directly.

SUB_NAV_ITEM_STATE.DESCRIPTION: Internal state inputs of hub-nav-item: nesting depth, active and expanded flags, and forced accordion behaviour inside mobile or panel contexts. hub-nav-item-list carries depth and forceAccordionMode too, so a whole level can be forced at once.

SUB_ITEM_LIST_ITEMS.DESCRIPTION: Items rendered by the internal hub-nav-item-list child. Managed automatically by hub-nav.

SUB_PANELS.DESCRIPTION: Stack of open panel states rendered by the internal hub-nav-panel-container in panel expand mode.

SUB_PANEL.DESCRIPTION: State of a single drill-down panel rendered by the internal hub-nav-panel child.

SUB_FORWARDED.DESCRIPTION: Internal wiring inputs the root hub-nav forwards to its children; each exists on the subset of these components that needs it, and isLast marks the outermost panel of a stack so it can close the stack's edge. Configure them through the config input on hub-nav instead of binding them directly.

SUB_OVERLAY_CLASSES.DESCRIPTION: Overlay wiring the root hub-nav forwards when submenus render in a body-level overlay: overlayOwnerClass is the unique class that ties an overlay back to its nav for outside-click handling, and overlayOrientationClass carries the nav's orientation so the host-context styles still apply outside the component tree.

CONFIG_ACTIVE_INDICATOR.DESCRIPTION: Whether the active mark travels between items instead of appearing and disappearing in place. Off by default; honours prefers-reduced-motion.

CONFIG_FOLLOW_REPLACED_URLS.DESCRIPTION: How eagerly the nav follows a scroll spy, which reports the reader position by replacing the URL: true follows each report, a number of milliseconds follows only once they go quiet, false never follows.

SUB_PANEL_CONTAINER_EVENTS.DESCRIPTION: Emitted by the internal hub-nav-panel-container with the panel id, relaying close (panelClose) and back (panelBack) requests to hub-nav.

Set the app-wide default through HubPanelsConfig.togglePosition.

PANELS_VARIANT.DESCRIPTION: hub-panels: semantic accent of the navigation strip — the active/hover tab, the active pill and the active accordion header all follow it. The built-in values ('primary' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'warning' | 'info') use the design-system tints, but any string is accepted: the strip reads --hub-sys-color-<variant> from your application. PRESET_CATALOGUE.TITLE: Preset Catalogue
PRESET_CATALOGUE.DESCRIPTION: The bundled catalogue is intentionally broad because loading states are usually repeated business UI, not isolated placeholders. It includes card, list-item, table-row, detail-view, form-section, dashboard-widget, stat-card, chart-panel, profile-summary, master-detail, kanban-card, feed-item, search-result, table-toolbar, filter-bar and empty-state-skeleton. The idea is to let teams start from a production-oriented loading vocabulary instead of rebuilding the same shimmer blocks in every feature. In practice, that means table-heavy screens can start from `table-toolbar` plus repeated `table-row`, dashboard screens can mix `stat-card`, `chart-panel` and `dashboard-widget`, and content-led flows can reach for `card`, `feed-item` or `search-result` without writing new layout markup from scratch.

COMPACT_DSL_AUTHORING.TITLE: Compact DSL Authoring
COMPACT_DSL_AUTHORING.DESCRIPTION: Inline templates use a compact Emmet-like syntax because the library optimizes for fast iteration inside Angular codebases. Sibling composition uses `+`, nesting uses `>`, modifiers live inside parentheses, repeats use `*N`, and params are interpolated with `{{param}}`. That gives teams a compact authoring surface that still reads well in pull requests and allows small changes without rewriting a full object tree. The important point is not syntax cleverness: it is that layout intent stays close to the component usage and remains simple to diff, refactor and review.

VARIANTS_AND_RESPONSIVE_LAYOUTS.TITLE: Variants And Responsive Layouts
VARIANTS_AND_RESPONSIVE_LAYOUTS.DESCRIPTION: Loading states should not ignore layout density or breakpoints, because users notice when the skeleton bears no relation to the real UI. Presets can expose variants such as `compact`, and individual modifier values can switch across breakpoints using compact responsive tokens. That makes it possible to keep one semantic skeleton definition while adapting widths, column counts, spacing and sizing across mobile, tablet and desktop contexts. The practical result is fewer duplicated templates and much better alignment between the placeholder phase and the real rendered interface.

PROGRAMMATIC_REGISTRATION_AND_THEMING.TITLE: Programmatic Registration And Theming
PROGRAMMATIC_REGISTRATION_AND_THEMING.DESCRIPTION: Bundled presets are the starting point, not the ceiling. Teams can register project-specific presets through Angular dependency injection and then consume them by name exactly like the built-in catalogue, which is critical when a product has its own repeated skeleton language. Visual tuning stays in CSS variables, so shimmer intensity, base colour, highlight colour, spacing and radius can align with the design system instead of leaking hardcoded values into feature components. This separation is important: structure belongs in presets and DSL, while visual policy belongs in theming.

OPTIONS.DESCRIPTION: Full SortableJS options object. Every SortableJS option can also be bound directly as its own input (for example `handle`, `animation` or `group`).

SORT.DESCRIPTION: Enables or disables reordering of items within the list.

DELAY.DESCRIPTION: Milliseconds the pointer must be held down before a drag may start. `0` by default; raise it on touch so a short press scrolls instead of dragging.

DISABLED.DESCRIPTION: Disables the sortable behaviour without removing the directive.

DRAGGABLE.DESCRIPTION: CSS selector that restricts which child elements can be dragged.

HANDLE.DESCRIPTION: CSS selector of the element inside each item that starts the drag, leaving the rest interactive.

ANIMATION.DESCRIPTION: Duration in milliseconds of the reordering animation.

GHOST_CLASS.DESCRIPTION: CSS class applied to the drop placeholder shown while dragging.

CHOSEN_CLASS.DESCRIPTION: CSS class applied to the item from the moment it is chosen until the drag ends. `sortable-chosen` by default.

DRAG_CLASS.DESCRIPTION: CSS class applied to the element that follows the pointer while dragging. `sortable-drag` by default.

FALLBACK_TOLERANCE.DESCRIPTION: Pixels the pointer must travel before the fallback drag begins. `0` by default; raise it so a tap is not read as a drag.

FALLBACK_CLASS.DESCRIPTION: CSS class applied to the cloned preview element used when the native HTML5 drag-and-drop is bypassed.

FALLBACK_OFFSET.DESCRIPTION: Pixel offset applied to the fallback drag preview relative to the pointer.

FORCE_FALLBACK.DESCRIPTION: Ignores the browser's native HTML5 drag-and-drop and always drags a clone, which looks the same in every browser.

FILTER.DESCRIPTION: CSS selector (or predicate) marking elements that cannot be dragged.

PREVENT_ON_FILTER.DESCRIPTION: Calls `preventDefault()` on the event that triggered `filter`. `true` by default; turn it off when the filtered element is a control that still needs its own click.

DIRECTION.DESCRIPTION: Axis the list is laid out along. Detected automatically when unset; set it explicitly for grids and wrapped lists, where the detection can guess wrong.

SWAP_THRESHOLD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of a target item (0 to 1) the pointer must cover before the two swap. `1` by default; lower values swap earlier.

INVERT_SWAP.DESCRIPTION: Always uses the inverted swap zone, so the swap happens as the pointer leaves an item instead of as it enters.

INVERTED_SWAP_THRESHOLD.DESCRIPTION: Threshold used while the swap zone is inverted. Falls back to `swapThreshold` when unset.

REMOVE_CLONE_ON_HIDE.DESCRIPTION: Removes the clone from the DOM while it is hidden instead of only hiding it. `true` by default.

IGNORE.DESCRIPTION: CSS selector for elements inside an item that must never start a drag, such as inputs or links.

TOUCH_START_THRESHOLD.DESCRIPTION: Pixels the finger may move before a delayed drag is cancelled — the margin between a drag and a scroll.

EMPTY_INSERT_THRESHOLD.DESCRIPTION: Distance in pixels from an empty list at which the dragged item is inserted into it. `5` by default; `0` requires the pointer to be inside the list.

DRAGOVER_BUBBLE.DESCRIPTION: Lets the dragover event keep propagating to ancestor elements.

SET_DATA.DESCRIPTION: Called when the drag starts to write onto the native `DataTransfer` — the hook for dragging out of the page.

UNCHOOSE.DESCRIPTION: Emitted when an item is released without being dragged.

SHOW_VALUE.DESCRIPTION: Whether the rounded percentage is rendered next to the bar.

LABEL.DESCRIPTION: Accessible label describing what the progress bar measures.

VALUE.DESCRIPTION: Current measurement, expressed on the [min, max] scale.

LOW.DESCRIPTION: Upper limit of the "low" region; defaults to min when omitted.

HIGH.DESCRIPTION: Lower limit of the "high" region; defaults to max when omitted.

OPTIMUM.DESCRIPTION: Preferred point of the range; defaults to the midpoint when omitted.

LABEL.DESCRIPTION: Accessible label naming what the gauge measures; role=meter takes its name from the author, so the meter is unnamed without it.

VALUE.DESCRIPTION: Score value, expressed as a 0..1 ratio or a 0..max figure.

MAX.DESCRIPTION: Upper bound the value is normalized against.

SIZE.DESCRIPTION: Outer diameter of the ring (number is treated as px, or any CSS length string), applied inline when set. Omit it to let the --hub-ring-size token drive the diameter.

THICKNESS.DESCRIPTION: Stroke width of the ring (number is treated as px, or any CSS length string), applied inline when set. Omit it to let the --hub-ring-thickness token drive the stroke.

THRESHOLDS.DESCRIPTION: Optional colour thresholds recolouring the indicator by band (low/high).

SHOW_VALUE.DESCRIPTION: Whether the rounded percentage is rendered in the centre.

LABEL.DESCRIPTION: Accessible label naming what the ring scores; neither the projected caption nor the centred percentage can name a role=meter.

CAPTION.DESCRIPTION: Content projected into the ring centre as a caption, rendered alongside (or instead of) the built-in percentage. It is decoration, not a name: an element with role="meter" is named by its author, so pass the `label` input.

INLINE_BLOCK.TITLE: Inline Block
INLINE_BLOCK.DESCRIPTION: `inline` is the default mode because a region that is still empty should already reserve the space its content will take: the block joins normal document flow, so nothing jumps when the real content arrives. `message` renders under the indicator, and anything projected between the tags renders under the message — the place for a cancel action or a note that the operation is taking longer than usual. The host carries `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-busy="true"`, so a screen reader picks the message up as it appears without interrupting whatever it is already reading.
INLINE_BLOCK.HIGHLIGHT: A block that takes part in normal flow and reserves the space the pending content will occupy, with a message and projected content under the indicator.

INDICATORS_AND_ACCENTS.TITLE: Indicators And Accents
INDICATORS_AND_ACCENTS.DESCRIPTION: Five pure-CSS indicators ship with the library — `spinner`, `dots`, `bars`, `pulse` and `ring` — so it pulls in no image asset and no icon font. Three size steps preset `--hub-loading-size`, and the token stays overridable on its own for a layout the steps do not cover. `color` is not an ordinary CSS colour: it goes through `resolveHubAccent()`, which reads a bare name such as `primary` as a design-system token that follows the theme, while a hex, an `oklch()` literal or a `var(...)` reference is used verbatim.
INDICATORS_AND_ACCENTS.HIGHLIGHT: Five pure-CSS indicators in three size steps, tinted by an accent that resolves a semantic name to a theme token and passes any CSS colour literal through untouched.

OVERLAY_AND_FULLSCREEN.TITLE: Overlay And Fullscreen
OVERLAY_AND_FULLSCREEN.DESCRIPTION: `overlay` covers one region instead of the page. It is positioned absolutely, so the nearest positioned ancestor decides what gets covered — give that container `position: relative`, or the overlay escapes upwards to whatever ancestor happens to be positioned. Scoping it that way keeps the rest of the screen scrollable and usable. `fullscreen` is fixed to the viewport and is what `HubLoadingService` mounts on `document.body`, outside every component subtree, so no ancestor's `overflow` or stacking context can clip it. Both modes paint the translucent scrim unless `backdrop` is turned off.
OVERLAY_AND_FULLSCREEN.HIGHLIGHT: Cover one positioned container and leave the rest of the page usable, or take the whole viewport through a service that mounts the overlay outside every component subtree.

BRANDING_AND_THEMING.TITLE: Branding And Theming
BRANDING_AND_THEMING.DESCRIPTION: `image` swaps the built-in indicator for a mark of your own, animated with `none`, `spin` or `pulse`: `spin` only reads well on a radially symmetric mark, while `pulse` keeps a wordmark upright and legible. Everything visual lives in the `--hub-loading-*` tokens, declared on `:where(.hub-loading)` so any ancestor can set them — accent, size, speed, stroke thickness, gap, image size, text colour, and the backdrop tint and blur. The `hub-loading-theme()` Sass mixin sets the whole ladder in one call, and `provideHubLoading()` re-bases the defaults for an entire application without touching a template.
BRANDING_AND_THEMING.HIGHLIGHT: Replace the indicator with a brand mark, and retheme accent, size, speed and backdrop through the `--hub-loading-*` tokens or the one-call `hub-loading-theme()` Sass mixin.

PAGE_PROGRESS_BAR.TITLE: Page Progress Bar
PAGE_PROGRESS_BAR.DESCRIPTION: `hub-loading-bar` is the thin strip that reports the page itself is on its way — the one under the navbar. Three decisions make it believable. It counts its callers, so a navigation and the three requests the page fires are four references and the bar finishes when the last one does, not the first. It waits before painting anything: work that finishes inside the grace period never shows a bar at all, because a 40 ms route that flashes a progress bar reads as a glitch rather than as speed. And its trickle decelerates as it fills, stopping short of the end — nothing here knows the real percentage, so only `complete()` may show 100%, because only `complete()` knows it is true. Place it with `mode="overlay"` inside a positioned navbar, or `mode="fixed"` and `--hub-loading-bar-offset` when the navbar is fixed too.
PAGE_PROGRESS_BAR.HIGHLIGHT: The strip under the navbar, wired to the router and to HttpClient, that waits before it appears and never claims to be finished until it is.

MODE.DESCRIPTION: Where the block sits. `inline` takes part in normal document flow and reserves its own space; `overlay` is positioned absolutely and covers the nearest positioned ancestor; `fullscreen` is fixed to the viewport.

VARIANT.DESCRIPTION: Which pure-CSS indicator to render. Ignored while `image` is set, since the image replaces the built-in indicator.

IMAGE.DESCRIPTION: URL or data URI rendered instead of the built-in indicator, typically a brand mark. Its box is sized by `--hub-loading-image-size`.

IMAGE_ANIMATION.DESCRIPTION: Motion applied to `image`, and inert while no image is set. `spin` suits a radially symmetric mark, `pulse` keeps a wordmark upright and legible, and `none` leaves it still.

MESSAGE.DESCRIPTION: Text rendered below the indicator, and what the live region announces when the block appears. `null` renders no message.

SIZE.DESCRIPTION: Size step feeding `--hub-loading-size`. The token stays overridable on its own when a layout needs a size the three steps do not cover.

COLOR.DESCRIPTION: Accent for the indicator, normalised by `resolveHubAccent()` into the single `--hub-loading-accent` slot. A bare name such as `primary` resolves to a `--hub-sys-color-*` token and follows the theme; a hex, an `oklch()` literal or a `var(...)` reference is used verbatim. `null` leaves the token's own cascade default in place.

BACKDROP.DESCRIPTION: Paints the translucent scrim over the covered content. Ignored in `inline` mode, which covers nothing.

ARIA_LABEL.DESCRIPTION: Accessible name announced by the host's `role="status"` live region.

BAR_MODE.DESCRIPTION: Where the strip sits. `inline` takes part in normal flow and reserves its own row, so nothing shifts when the bar appears; `overlay` is positioned absolutely against the nearest positioned ancestor — the navbar you gave `position: relative`; `fixed` pins it to the viewport at `--hub-loading-bar-offset`.

BAR_PLACEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Which edge the `overlay` and `fixed` modes attach to. `bottom` is what hangs the bar off the underside of a navbar; `inline` ignores it.

BAR_PROGRESS.DESCRIPTION: Takes the bar over. Left unbound it follows `HubLoadingBarService`; a number from 0 to 100 drives it directly and is published as `aria-valuenow`; `null` hides it.

BAR_INDETERMINATE.DESCRIPTION: Sweeps a fragment back and forth instead of filling, for work with no measurable progress. The announced value is withheld, which is how ARIA marks a progressbar of unknown position.

BAR_GLOW.DESCRIPTION: Soft glow trailing the leading edge — the detail that still reads as movement between trickle ticks.

BAR_COLOR.DESCRIPTION: Accent for the fill. A bare name resolves to a `--hub-sys-color-*` token and follows the theme; a hex, an `oklch()` or a `var(...)` is used verbatim.

SHOW.DESCRIPTION: Registers one caller and mounts the fullscreen overlay if it is not up yet. Only the keys actually supplied are applied over the application defaults, so nested calls compose instead of resetting each other.

HIDE.DESCRIPTION: Retires one caller and tears the overlay down once none are left. The counter is clamped at zero, so a stray `hide()` cannot turn a later `show()` into a no-op.

HIDE_ALL.DESCRIPTION: Drops every pending caller at once and removes the overlay immediately. An escape hatch for error handlers and route changes, not a substitute for balanced `show()` / `hide()` pairs.

UPDATE.DESCRIPTION: Re-dresses the live overlay — a progress message that changes mid-operation, a variant swap — without touching the reference counter.

IS_LOADING.DESCRIPTION: Signal that is true while at least one caller is still waiting. Safe to read during server-side rendering, where the counter runs but no overlay is mounted.

BAR_START.DESCRIPTION: Registers one caller. The first begins a cycle — after the grace period, not immediately — and the rest simply join the count.

BAR_COMPLETE.DESCRIPTION: Retires one caller. Once none are left the bar runs to 100% and fades away, or disappears unseen if the grace period swallowed the whole operation.

BAR_COMPLETE_ALL.DESCRIPTION: Drops every pending caller and completes the bar at once. For an error handler, or a caller that never balanced its `start()`.

BAR_SET.DESCRIPTION: Moves the bar to an exact value and reveals it without waiting out the grace period. For work whose percentage is real; the value is clamped to 0–100 but not to the trickle ceiling.

BAR_INC.DESCRIPTION: Advances the bar and reveals it. Without an amount the configured trickle curve decides, which is what keeps an unknown wait moving without ever arriving.

BAR_RESET.DESCRIPTION: Cancels everything at once — no completion animation, no pending callers, nothing on screen.

BAR_PROGRESS.DESCRIPTION: Current fill, 0–100. Safe to read during server-side rendering.

BAR_IS_ACTIVE.DESCRIPTION: Whether any caller is still waiting — the honest “is the page loading?” question, regardless of whether the bar has decided to show itself.

BAR_IS_VISIBLE.DESCRIPTION: Whether the bar is actually painted. False during the grace period, and still true through the completion tail.

0.NAME: Default Content Slot
0.DESCRIPTION: Anything projected between the tags renders below the message — a cancel action, a progress note, or a hint that the operation is taking longer than usual.

1.DESCRIPTION: Registers application-wide defaults through the `HUB_LOADING_CONFIG` token — brand image, preferred variant, translated label — so `<hub-loading>` and `HubLoadingService` both start from them and individual call sites stay bare.

2.NAME: Bar Under The Navbar
2.DESCRIPTION: The placement the bar is named after. `position: relative` on the navbar is what confines the overlay to it, and `placement="bottom"` hangs it off the lower edge.

3.DESCRIPTION: Runs the bar for exactly the length of a navigation, including one a guard rejects or an error ends — the two cases that normally strand a hand-wired bar.

4.DESCRIPTION: Holds the bar open for the lifetime of every HTTP request. `finalize` balances it on success, on error and on cancellation alike.

5.DESCRIPTION: Takes one request out of the count. A poll on a timer would otherwise hold the bar open forever, and a progress bar that never finishes is worse than none.

6.DESCRIPTION: Registers application-wide bar defaults through the `HUB_LOADING_BAR_CONFIG` token — accent, pacing, grace period, trickle curve, translated label.

INDICATOR_VARIANTS.DESCRIPTION: The five bundled indicators, the three size steps, and the three shapes an accent can take — a semantic name, a CSS colour literal and a `var(...)` reference.

CONTAINER_OVERLAY.DESCRIPTION: An overlay confined to one card by that card's `position: relative`, leaving the rest of the page scrollable. Toggle the backdrop to see the difference between a background refresh and work that invalidates what is on screen.

FULLSCREEN_SERVICE.TITLE: Fullscreen Service
FULLSCREEN_SERVICE.DESCRIPTION: `HubLoadingService` driven from TypeScript. Two overlapping requests show why the reference counter matters: the first `hide()` leaves the overlay up because the second caller still holds a reference, and `update()` rewrites the message mid-flight.

BRANDED_IMAGE.TITLE: Branded Image
BRANDED_IMAGE.DESCRIPTION: A brand mark replacing the built-in indicator, shown with each of the three image animations so the trade-off between `spin`, `pulse` and `none` is visible.

CSS_VARIABLES.TITLE: CSS Variable Theming
CSS_VARIABLES.DESCRIPTION: Live theming through the `--hub-loading-*` tokens set on a wrapper element, including the backdrop tint and blur that only do anything in `overlay` and `fullscreen` modes.

PAGE_PROGRESS.TITLE: Page Progress Bar
PAGE_PROGRESS.DESCRIPTION: The bar hanging off a mock navbar. Three routes show the three behaviours: an ordinary one trickles, a slow one shows the trickle decelerating, and a 40 ms one never paints a bar at all.

DETERMINATE_BAR.TITLE: Known And Unknown Progress
DETERMINATE_BAR.DESCRIPTION: Binding `progress` hands the bar to the caller and publishes `aria-valuenow`; `indeterminate` sweeps instead and withholds it. The third state, `null`, puts the bar away.

ROUTER_HTTP_BAR.TITLE: Router And HTTP Wiring
ROUTER_HTTP_BAR.DESCRIPTION: Why the bar counts its callers: a navigation plus three requests are four references, and the bar finishes when the last one does. The code shows `provideHubLoadingBarRouter()`, the interceptor and the opt-out.

RTL_SWEEP.TITLE: Sweeping Right to Left
RTL_SWEEP.DESCRIPTION: The same `indeterminate` bar under `dir="ltr"` and under `dir="rtl"`. The sweep reverses with the text, driven by `--hub-loading-bar-sweep-direction`, so nothing has to be bound or duplicated per locale.

ONE_COMMAND.TITLE: One Command
ONE_COMMAND.DESCRIPTION: `ng add ng-hub-ui` is the whole installation. The Angular CLI fetches the package, runs its `ng-add` schematic, and the schematic asks which of the 25 catalogued libraries you want. Space selects, `a` toggles everything, `i` inverts the selection; confirming resolves the choice into npm packages, writes them into `dependencies` and hands the install to whichever package manager the CLI detected.
ONE_COMMAND.HIGHLIGHT: One `ng add`, a multi-select of the 25 catalogued libraries, and the packages land in your manifest.

SCRIPTABLE.TITLE: Flags And Scripts
SCRIPTABLE.DESCRIPTION: The prompt is skippable, which is what makes the installer usable from CI and from a project's own setup script. `--libraries` accepts a comma-separated list or the same flag repeated, and both forms normalize identically: trimmed, de-duplicated, in the order they were given. `--skip-install` writes the manifest and stops there. Pass the identifiers from the catalogue, not the labels the prompt renders — they are different strings, and an unknown one stops the schematic before `package.json` is touched.
SCRIPTABLE.HIGHLIGHT: `--libraries` in either form and `--skip-install`, so a workspace can be set up from a script instead of by hand.

RESOLVED_DEPENDENCIES.TITLE: Resolved Dependencies
RESOLVED_DEPENDENCIES.DESCRIPTION: A selection is not the list of packages that gets written. Each catalogued library names the peers it needs — `ng-hub-ui-utils` for most of the family, `ng-hub-ui-ds` for panels, `ng-hub-ui-forms` for signature, and `sortablejs`, which is not ours at all — and resolution is transitive, so a co-installed library contributes its own peers in turn. Every range floors at or above the highest peer the family declares on it, which is what keeps the write from producing a pair npm cannot satisfy. A key already present is never rewritten, so a version you have pinned survives. The schematic stops at dependency wiring: no `angular.json`, no providers, no component registrations, no stylesheet entries.
RESOLVED_DEPENDENCIES.HIGHLIGHT: Peers pulled in automatically and transitively, every range floored above what the family demands, and a version you pinned left alone.

INTERACTIVE.TITLE: Interactive install
INTERACTIVE.DESCRIPTION: The command and the prompt it opens, as they appear in the terminal.

NON_INTERACTIVE.TITLE: Flags instead of the prompt
NON_INTERACTIVE.DESCRIPTION: The three non-interactive forms, and the two ways a bad selection is refused.

RESOLVED_DEPENDENCIES.DESCRIPTION: Two libraries asked for, five packages written — the co-installs made concrete.
